transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-07-08 | Time: 11:00 AM ET | Duration: ~50m | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Jake (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood SE), Karen Liu (Haven InfoSec), Tom Alvarez (Platform Eng), Maya Singh (PM), Ben Carter (Compliance)

[00:00] Samira (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining the weekly security sync, hope y'all had a good week. quick recap, we shipped the latest logging agent for the hosted pilot and pushed the retention config that Tom asked for.

[00:18] Karen (Haven): yeah thanks, a few items we want to validate today: SSO flow with Okta, how audit logs look and whether they can be forwarded to our Splunk instance, and confirmation on retention/deletion for PII. also where we stand on SOC2 evidence.

[00:34] Jake (Redwood SE): great, i'll take the SSO bit first. we configured SAML with the test tenant you shared, there were a couple of attribute mapping quirks — email vs userprincipalname — that we noted. tom, when you set up the test app could you include both attributes so we can verify mapping?

[00:50] Tom (Haven): sure, i can add that. question on assertion lifetime — is there a session length requirement on your side?

[00:58] Jake: no hard requirement, we honor the assertion but default token lifetime on the platform is one hour for the pilot. we can extend for staging. also note that the cloud SSO metadata URL has an automated refresh; if you pin metadata you'll need to update manually.

[01:18] Karen: perfect. next, on audit logs — can you confirm what fields are included and whether we can export raw logs to our SIEM? we need object-level events and user identifiers for our audit trail.

[01:30] Luis (Redwood): yes we capture admin actions, token issuance, model invocation events, and config changes. right now hosted pilot supports log forwarding via syslog/HTTPS to third-party SIEMs. i'll send a sample export showing schema, timestamps, and the user id fields. caveat: some fields are pseudonymized by default for hosted deployments unless you opt into full-event export.

[01:52] Ben (Haven): pseudonymized how? we need to be able to map to internal user ids for audit.

[01:58] Luis: the default anonymization replaces full email addresses with hashed identifiers; we can enable a customer-managed option that preserves usernames if you sign the additional data access addendum for the pilot. Jake and i will include the exact switch in the docs.

[02:18] Maya (Haven): on data retention — our baseline requirement is 90 days for logs and 7 years for certain financial records. for pilot purposes can we get 90 days and then discuss archiving?

[02:30] Samira: yes that's doable as a pilot config. for longer retention, we recommend exporting logs to your cold storage or enabling long-term archive which we can configure on Dedicated or Private. for hosted there's an add-on archival flow.

[02:46] Karen: SOC2 — we reviewed the pack you sent last week, can you provide the latest control matrix and POC artifacts? we need to map to our vendor risk questionnaire.

[02:58] Samira: absolutely i'll send the SOC2 summary and a redwood security pack (redacted evidence pointers) by Friday. keep in mind the full SOC2 report is under NDA; we have an extract that covers relevant sections for vendor reviews.

[03:12] Tom: KMS integration — how does key management look for hosted? we prefer customer-managed keys if possible.

[03:20] Luis: for hosted we support bring-your-own key via our KMS integration pattern; however, in the pilot it's a bit more constrained. we can simulate customer-managed keys for encryption at rest, or provide HSM-backed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments. we'll document the IAM roles and the handshake flow.

[03:38] Karen: and audit logging for KMS operations? we need to ensure key access is auditable.

[03:42] Luis: yes key access events are surfaced in the audit stream; when you enable customer KMS you'll see the KMS event markers in the log export.

[03:50] Jake: one subtlety — model KV cache and request-level caching may surface as additional events; sometimes the transcripting picks up KV as K V or K V cash in our logs, so we've added clearer event names in the sample.

[04:06] Maya: small question — retention of model outputs; do you store user prompts and generated text?

[04:12] Samira: by default we retain request metadata and hashes of prompt/response for 90 days in the pilot; full-text retention is off unless you enable it. for customers that need full-text for compliance we do a separate addendum and we recommend Private deployment.

[04:30] Ben: liability question — if a user uploads PII and it remains in logs, what's the purge flow?

[04:36] Jake: there's a deletion API we can call to remove artifacts, and we have retention policies that trigger automatic deletion. we'll share the API docs and a sample purge run. note deletion in backups may take longer — we'll include RTO/RPO expectations.

[04:58] Karen: ok, sounds good. two more quick items — SSO test plan and timeline, and whether you can push a sample audit export to our Splunk test endpoint this week.

[05:08] Tom: i'll create the Okta app today and invite the redwood test user.

[05:12] Samira: perfect. action items recap: i'll send SOC2 extract/security pack; jake/luis will send audit log sample and KMS doc; tom will set up Okta test app; luis will open the KMS support ticket. any blockers?

[05:28] Karen: the only blocker is us getting the audit sample and an example of the user mapping so our GRC team can sign off.

[05:34] Samira: we'll prioritize that and aim to deliver by Monday/Tuesday next week.

[05:40] Maya: one ask — can you include a line in the sample that shows how role-based access (RBAC) maps to actions? our auditors want to see "who did what" in a clear way.

[05:48] Jake: yes we'll include RBAC mapping in the audit sample and highlight principal identifiers.

[05:54] Samira: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and book the final pilot wrap for week of the 20th. thanks for joining.

[06:02] Karen: thanks all.

End of transcript.
